newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan offers rebate to draw foreign airlines.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan offers rebate to draw foreign airlines.

text.p: The Pakistani cabinet decided on Monday to allow a 50 percent rebate in aeronautical charges for one year to attract new airlines to use Pakistan's airports.

A cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto "approved various proposals to attract foreign airlines to use Pakistani airports more frequently as one of their destinations or transit points," a government statement said.

Last month, the cabinet approved a proposal to review bilateral air service agreements with important countries to make them more liberal on a reciprocal basis and permit a gradual access to northern airports to foreign airlines.
Monday's meeting "decided to allow a 50 percent rebate for one year in all aeronautical charges to all new or restarting airlines", the government statement said.
"This incentive will, however, not be available to airlines presently operating services to or from Pakistan," it said.
In 1994, Bhutto's government scrapped a short-lived open sky policy that allowed foreign airlines free access to Pakistani airports without reciprocal arrangements.

The policy, part of an economic liberalisation programme of former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, was cancelled after protests from the state-run Pakistan International Airlines, which said it had suffered huge losses in one year when at least six foreign airlines started flying to Pakistan without reciprocal arrangements.
